items.title: Ex-commando loses battle with leukaemia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former commando Sergeant Mohd Azuan Asmuni, whose battle with leukaemia drew the personal attention of Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, has died after a prolonged fight against the disease. Azuan, a former member of the 11th Special Service Regiment (11 SSR), died on Monday after being diagnosed with Acute Myeloid Leukaemia in 2023. Despite undergoing various treatments, Malek said Azuan had shown remarkable fighting spirit and resilience throughout his illness.

items.title: MEF: Faster aid needed before viable MSMEs are forced to close
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must move faster to support viable micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) facing mounting cost and cash-flow pressures, or risk seeing temporary business difficulties turn into permanent closures and job losses. Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) president Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said many MSMEs were not seeking permanent subsidies or special treatment, but simply needed enough "breathing space" to navigate a challenging operating environment. Syed Hussain said the consequences of a viable MSME shutting down extended beyond the business owner.

items.title: National Day, Malaysia Day corporate sponsorship surges to RM48.63mil, up 118pct
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Corporate and private sector support for this year's National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations has more than doubled to RM48.63 million, up 118 per cent from RM22.3 million last year. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the increase reflected growing private sector commitment to the celebrations. Fahmi said 5GB would be provided on National Day on Aug 31 and another 5GB on Malaysia Day on Sept 16.

items.title: Immigration blames airline systems for long-validity passport headaches
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Difficulties experienced by holders of Malaysian International Passports (PMA) with validity periods exceeding 10 years while travelling abroad were caused by systems used by certain airlines, rather than the immigration control systems of foreign countries, according to the Immigration Department. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said that, in terms of border controls and International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards, passports with validity periods exceeding 10 years did not pose a problem. Zakaria said the issue involved, among other things, systems used by airlines that set the maximum passport validity period at 10 years.

items.title: Haze hits Malaysia as 12 air monitoring stations record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Malaysia has been experiencing haze since Aug 8, with 11 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and one station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading as of 3pm today, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said. In a statement today, the ministry said the El Niño phenomenon occurring alongside the Southwest Monsoon had resulted in several areas, particularly southern Peninsular Malaysia and western and southern Sarawak, receiving below-average rainfall. As of 3pm today, 11 of the 68 air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings.

items.title: Tun M, Dr Siti Hasmah recognised as record-breaking centenarian couple
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, have made history after receiving three official records recognising their longevity and unprecedented achievements as a couple. Dr Mahathir, 101, was recognised by Asean Records as the Oldest Living Former Prime Minister, while Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, was named the Oldest Living Spouse of a Former Prime Minister. The couple were also jointly recognised by Asia Records as the First Former Head of Government and Spouse to Both Become Living Centenarians.

items.title: All parties must learn from past management weaknesses in TH, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All parties must learn from weaknesses and mistakes in the management of Lembaga Tabung Haji following the government's explanation in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government received various views, criticism, and condemnations from members of parliament during yesterday's special sitting. However, he said the government's intention during the special sitting was to clarify the RCI report to Parliament and the public, highlighting various issues involving governance and integrity within TH.

items.title: Couple charged in Ipoh court with trafficking MDMA
items.summary: IPOH: A married couple was charged in the magistrate's court today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine last week. Teoh Wai Loon, 44, and Lim Suk Pei, 38, nodded after the charge was read before magistrate S. Punitha. No plea was recorded as drug trafficking cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.

items.title: Police expedite aid for family of officer killed in Sabah electric shock accident
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Police will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died from electric shock last Thursday. He said today's visit to the family home was a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force. Accompanying him were Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat, and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin.

items.title: Airport security plan heads to Cabinet next week after Malaysian pilot's drug bust
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — A plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet next week following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia on suspicion of drug smuggling, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the matter was discussed at last week’s Cabinet meeting, which instructed all relevant regulatory agencies to draw up plans to strengthen airport security. The agencies included the Home Ministry, Transport Ministry, Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Aviation Security, Malaysia Aviation Commission (MAVCOM) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), he said.

items.title: Perak DAP backs staying in unity government until end of term
items.summary: IPOH: Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the unity government and mobilise the party's entire machinery to fulfil the people's mandate and continue the country's reform agenda. In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. "DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people's expectations.

items.title: Four company directors claim trial over alleged fake Perkeso claims
items.summary: Alpha Buildcon director Henry Ratnaike, 45, faces four charges, while PK Tan Auto and Car Repair director Koh Kai Loon, 40, faces one charge. Prima Kerjaya Trading director Gan Pay Kiat, 32, faces two charges, while fellow Alpha Buildcon director Ling Yate May, 58, faces four charges of abetting Henry. Henry allegedly committed the offences at Taman Merdeka Jaya, Batu Berendam, on May 10, 2024, while Koh allegedly committed his offence at Taman Kasawari Utama, Durian Tunggal, on June 14, 2024.

items.title: Malaysia, Saudi Arabia sign pact to share judicial know-how
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Saudi Arabia today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in the judicial field. The MoU was signed by Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia Azhaniz Teh Azman Teh and Saudi Arabian Minister of Justice Sheikh Dr Waleed Mohammed Alsmani at the Palace of Justice here. The MoU signing, witnessed by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, was held in conjunction with Sheikh Dr Waleed’s official visit to Malaysia.

items.title: Six express bus passengers injured in collision with trailer
items.summary: BANDAR BAHARU: Six passengers were injured when an express bus collided with a trailer at Km169.2 of the North-South Expressway early today. Bandar Baharu district police chief Superintendent Mohamad Sani Mat Ali said police received a call from the control room at 1.09am regarding the accident involving the two vehicles. He said preliminary investigations revealed that the express bus, carrying nine passengers, was travelling from Alor Star to Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Property crime pushes Pahang crime index higher in first seven months of 2026
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 12 — The Pahang crime index increased by 105 cases to 1,262 cases from January to July this year, compared to 1,157 cases for the same period last year. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the rate of resolving crime cases decreased to 59.58 per cent from 71.74 per cent. Azry Akmar said that although the number of commercial cases increased, the recorded loss value decreased 9.8 per cent to RM46.3 million, compared to RM51.3 million last year.

items.title: #NSTviral: Garbage truck crashes and lands on SUV at Pantai Hill Park
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A garbage truck crashed and landed on a parked SUV at Pantai Hill Park here. A social media post accompanying the video claimed that the truck driver, who is a foreigner, abandoned the vehicle and fled the scene. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Kedah PAS vows to continue fight against gambling after Federal Court ruling
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 12 — Kedah PAS today vowed to continue its efforts to eliminate gambling in the state despite the Federal Court dismissing the state government’s bid to appeal a ruling against its ban on issuing and renewing gambling premises licences. Kedah PAS commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party accepted the court’s decision but expressed disappointment over the outcome. “Kedah Pas takes note of the Federal Court’s decision to reject the Kedah government’s application for leave to appeal over the cessation of gambling premises licences.

items.title: Singaporean man, girlfriend rescued from kidnap-for-ransom syndicate
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police rescued two Singaporeans, including a man wanted by Singapore authorities, from a kidnap-for-ransom syndicate within 24 hours of receiving a report from the man's mother. Bukit Aman criminal investigation department director Datuk M Kumar said the 32-year-old man and his 28-year-old girlfriend were rescued near a supermarket in Nusa Bestari at 6pm yesterday. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Jadi's RM35mil warrant proceeds hang in balance as shares lag exercise price
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Jadi Imaging Holdings Bhd looks unlikely to realise nearly RM35 million in potential proceeds from 699.64 million warrants expiring next month, with its shares currently trading below the warrants' exercise price. The company said 699.64 million warrants remained outstanding as at Aug 6 and will expire at 5pm on Sept 14. At the five-sen exercise price, full conversion of the outstanding warrants could bring Jadi about RM34.98 million in fresh proceeds.

items.title: Two men jailed 14 days, fined RM8,000 each over fake MCs
items.summary: KUANTAN: Two men were sentenced to 14 days in jail and fined RM8,000 each after pleading guilty to forging 40 medical certificates, at the magistrate's court here today. Mohd Shukrie Zainuddin, 28, and Muhammad Asyraf Zunaidy, 31, will face an additional eight months in jail if they fail to pay the fine. Magistrate Ellyna Othman handed down the sentence after the duo admitted to forging medical certificates purportedly issued by a clinic, using a doctor's name and signature to deceive others.

items.title: Worried govt producing GMO rice? Agriculture Ministry says Perak run is only a controlled test
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 12 — The proposed genetically modified rice field trial in Perak involving the MR219 variety is only a controlled test plot and does not constitute approval for the use of genetically modified organism (GMO) crops in Malaysia, said Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak. He said the trial was intended to generate scientific evidence and data on GMO, particularly its potential role in addressing food security challenges, rather than to allow its commercial use. Isham assured that the test plot would be conducted under controlled, monitored and documented conditions to ensure that any potential issues would not spread beyond the trial area.

items.title: Japan brushes off Australian PM's melon drama
items.summary: TOKYO: Tokyo on Wednesday played down comments by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese about melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart that have triggered a row Down Under, stressing the leaders' good relationship. We have been informed by the Australian side that Prime Minister Albanese did not make the comments in the way that has been reported," a Japanese government statement said. It's disrespectful towards our prime minister," said one X user.

items.title: Anwar to meet Brunei Sultan next week for 27th Leaders' Consultation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will meet Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah in Bandar Seri Begawan next week for the 27th Annual Leaders' Consultation (ALC) between Malaysia and Brunei. Anwar said he received a telephone call from the Sultan, who asked about his wellbeing and prayed for his health. Anwar said he also prayed for the Sultan's continued good health and wellbeing.

items.title: RM200,000-plus aid for family of cop killed in Sabah electric shock incident, says home minister
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died in an electric shock incident in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday. He said today’s visit to the late officer’s family home, accompanied by Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, was also a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force. Saifuddin Nasution said the assistance presented included contributions from the Sabah and Kelantan Police Contingents (IPK), as well as takaful payments from the deceased’s contributions as a member of the Police Cooperative, with total contributions and payments exceeding RM200,000.

items.title: Putin threatens retaliatory seizures of European ships
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday threatened to seize ships belonging to European countries in retaliation for plans to sell off cargo seized from Russian "shadow fleet" vessels. Several European companies have intercepted ships carrying Russian oil in contravention of European sanctions targeting the vital revenue source. New sanctions passed last month permit EU members to sell the oil or any other cargo seized from the ships.

items.title: Court of Appeal says Malaysia is not the right forum for 1MDB suit against UK law firm White & Case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Court of Appeal today granted an appeal by UK law firm White & Case LLP against a High Court ruling that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia. In a unanimous decision, a three-judge panel chaired by Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, sitting with Justices K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, ruled that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm. The court ordered 1MDB to pay RM130,000 in costs to White & Case.

items.title: KLIA flights to be suspended during National Day flypast rehearsals
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Take-offs and landings at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) will be temporarily suspended during rehearsals and the National Day flypast as airspace within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area is closed on selected dates. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the airspace would be closed from Aug 26 to 29 and on Aug 31 to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day flypast in Putrajaya. Aug 31: National Day flypast from 8.45am to 9.45am.

items.title: Nanta to leave Parliament, eyes state assembly seat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi will not defend his Kapit parliamentary seat in the next general election (GE16). Nanta, who is also Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secretary-general, however said he would remain in politics. He plans to contest a new state assembly seat within the Kapit constituency if it is gazetted ahead of the next Sarawak election.

items.title: RM300mil paint shop puts Inokom in pole position for automotive growth
items.summary: INOKOM Corp Sdn Bhd has strengthened its manufacturing capabilities with the launch of Paint Shop 3 (PS3), a RM300 million investment aimed at boosting production capacity, technology transfer and sustainable automotive manufacturing in Malaysia. "Inokom has evolved alongside the National Automotive Policy," said Inokom director Tan Sri Ben Yeoh. "PS3 is a significant enhancement to Inokom's manufacturing ecosystem.

items.title: Navigating choppy geopolitics requires a multi-faceted strategic balancing act
items.summary: UNVEILING the 13th Malaysia Plan in parliament on July 31st, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim underlined the importance of regional security to Malaysia's 2026-2030 development roadmap. He singled out the South China Sea, declaring that Malaysia's "readiness to confront sovereignty and security threats in the South China Sea will be intensified more comprehensively." Malaysia has also continued to deepen its defence cooperation and exchanges with Japan, another standout security partner.

items.title: Kedah Pas vows to continue fight against gambling despite court ruling
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Kedah Pas has vowed to continue its fight to eliminate gambling in the state despite the Federal Court's dismissal of the state government's bid to appeal a ruling against its ban on issuing and renewing gambling premises licences. Kedah Pas commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party accepted the court's decision, while expressing disappointment over the outcome. "Kedah Pas takes note of the Federal Court's decision to reject the Kedah government's application for leave to appeal over the cessation of gambling premises licences.

items.title: Teach children to speak up, disagree with respect, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Education should not merely teach children to be well-behaved, but also give them the confidence to speak up, think critically and disagree respectfully, says Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek. She said character education should equip students to articulate their views, challenge opposing opinions and defend their positions without compromising courtesy. Fadhlina said the forum demonstrated how young people could build confidence in using Bahasa Melayu while developing their ability to argue and engage with differing views.

items.title: Kelantan rewards Muay Thai fighter Aliff Rakib RM20,000 after ONE Championship triumph
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Muay Thai fighter Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib today received RM20,000 from the Kelantan government in recognition of his historic ONE Championship victory last month. The Rantau Panjang-born fighter, better known as Aliff Rakib, made history last month when he knocked out Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao in the fifth round at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok to win the ONE Interim Strawweight Muay Thai World Championship. The victory made Aliff the first Malaysian fighter to win a Muay Thai world championship belt in ONE Championship.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt raises RM48m in sponsorships for Merdeka, Malaysia Day celebrations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Sponsorships for this year’s Merdeka and Malaysia Day celebrations have risen to more than RM48 million, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced today, describing the contributions as a “public-private partnership” success. Of the total, RM2.7 million was contributed in cash, while the remaining RM45.93 million comprised contributions in the form of goods and services. “The ministry is deeply honoured to announce that the total value of sponsorship for HKHM 2026, as verified by the Ministry of Communications Sponsorship Committee to date, amounts to RM48.63 million,” the minister said at an event to celebrate the sponsors here.

items.title: Influencer avoids jail, bound over for promoting online gambling
items.summary: MARANG: A female influencer escaped a jail term after the magistrate's court here today ordered her to be bound over for good behaviour for two years on a RM2,000 bond after she pleaded guilty to promoting online gambling. Magistrate Nur Athirah Hashim imposed the order on Nur Syakilla Natasya Sukri, 20, after considering a Social Welfare Department report and submissions from the defence. The court was informed by Assistant Social Welfare Officer Shahrizal Ali that a social report was prepared because the accused, aged under 21, is classified as a young offender, to assist the court in evaluating her background and personal circumstances before sentencing.

items.title: Perak DAP says it will remain in unity govt, back Anwar’s reform agenda
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the Unity Government and mobilise the party’s entire machinery to fulfil the people’s mandate and continue the country’s reform agenda. In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people’s expectations.

items.title: Act now before haze turns into crisis – Lee Lam Thye
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must act early to prevent worsening transboundary haze from developing into a national crisis, says Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye. He said unhealthy air quality in parts of Sarawak and deteriorating conditions in parts of Peninsular Malaysia should serve as an early warning for the government to prepare for another serious haze episode. Lee said above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall forecast across parts of Southeast Asia could further increase the risk of fires and haze.

items.title: Kerjaya Prospek lands RM223mil Johor contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd has secured a RM223 million contract from Sunway Majestic Sdn Bhd to construct a 1,012-unit Small Office/Home Office development in Johor Bahru. The contract, awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd, covers the main building works for two 34-storey buildings, a 10-level podium car park and two levels of mezzanine commercial space. Kerjaya Prospek chief executive officer and executive director Tee Eng Tiong said the company's year-to-date FY26 contract wins have reached RM2.4 billion, exceeding its initial RM2 billion target for the year.

items.title: Three years on the run, Singaporean still eludes MACC despite 10-month promise
items.summary: x KUALA LUMPUR: A Singaporean man wanted by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) for the past three years remains untraceable despite promising 10 months ago to meet investigators. MACC said the Kuala Lumpur magistrate's court issued arrest warrants against the duo on Aug 4 after repeated attempts to locate them failed. Kok's last known Malaysian address is B-24-03, Abadi Villa, Jalan 3/109C, Off Jalan Klang Lama, Taman Abadi Indah, Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Kelantan sets up vehicle to tap oil and gas sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kelantan state government has established a special purpose vehicle, Kelantan Ventures Sdn Bhd (KVSB), to strengthen the state's involvement in the oil and gas industry. Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said KVSB aims to ensure that the people could benefit from the initiative while contributing to the state's sustainable economic development. Fadzli added that the state government is building capacity, exploring investment opportunities and establishing partnerships with reputable companies across the industry's value chain.

items.title: Ipoh married couple charged with trafficking 480.6g MDMA, face death penalty
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 12 — A married couple was charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) last week. According to the charge, they were jointly accused of trafficking 480.6 grammes of MDMA at Room M333, The Pearl Orient Sdn Bhd, Bercham Bistari 4, Medan Bercham Bistari, in the Kinta district, at about 10.30 pm on Aug 4. During the raids, police seized ketamine and MDMA, including about 2.6 kilogrammes of MDMA found at two houses in Tapah.

items.title: ACCCIM backs Building Managers Act as property management grows more complex
items.summary: The association said such developments require increasingly specialised management due to multiple ownership structures, different property uses and more sophisticated building systems. "This Act is overdue in light of the increasing development of stratified buildings and also the development of mixed-use integrated developments requiring more complex management of such buildings owned by multiple owners and integrated buildings of different usage. It said modern building management requires expertise across multiple disciplines, supported by continuous training and professional development to keep pace with evolving industry requirements.

items.title: Malaysia brings foreign ambassadors to Sabah’s east coast to boost security confidence, tourism
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The government is taking a direct approach to rebuilding international confidence in Sabah’s east coast by bringing foreign ambassadors and representatives to assess the security situation firsthand, almost 13 years after the Lahad Datu incident. He said the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM), which covers 10 districts along Sabah’s east coast and brings together three main agencies, was responsible for ensuring that the security situation in the area returned to normal. Saifuddin Nasution said the area had vast tourism potential, with its islands, beaches, rivers and forests contributing to local economic activities.

items.title: Maritime expert: Port businesses hit hard by uncertainty over commingled oil tax
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Businesses involved in the shipping and petroleum sectors are being badly affected by uncertainty over the tax treatment of oil cargo commingled in shore tanks at Johor’s Tanjung Langsat Port, said Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy. With more than 30 years of maritime experience, Jeyenderan said the issue was particularly important at Tanjung Langsat Port, where petroleum cargo is handled and may be discharged from vessels into shore tanks during transshipment operations. “Customs needed to establish clear requirements covering documentation, cargo classification, valuation and tax assessment to ensure businesses knew exactly what was expected of them.

items.title: Sarawak caregiver in the dock over fractured arm of baby just 20 days old
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 12 — A 29-year-old woman claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of causing injury to a 20-day-old baby at a confinement centre here last week. The accused, from Puncak Borneo, pleaded not guilty before Judge Noorhisham Mohd Jaafar after she was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611). The charge alleged that the accused, who was entrusted with the care of the baby, had negligently handled and lifted the child from a baby cot in a manner likely to cause physical injury.

items.title: Hainan, here we come: Penang gets new direct China flight in Oct
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 12 — The Haikou-Penang direct flight service will be launched on Oct 11, making Haikou the ninth Chinese city to have a scheduled direct air link with Penang, said State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai. He said the new route would further strengthen air connectivity between Hainan and Penang while opening up greater opportunities for Penang to tap into the China tourism market. “Haikou will become the ninth Chinese city with a scheduled direct air connection to Penang, further strengthening Penang’s air connectivity with China.

items.title: Selangor wants one body to get Greater Klang Valley projects moving together
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor state government is streamlining its metropolitan governance model through the proposed establishment of the Selangor Metropolitan Corporation (PMS) to coordinate development planning across multiple local authority (PBT) jurisdictions. State Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said the proposal was part of the Selangor Greater Klang Valley (SGKV) initiative, with the PMS serving as the coordinating body for the planning, development and implementation of projects involving more than one PBT. “To support the implementation of the model, the state government proposes the establishment of PMS as a state-level coordinating mechanism.

items.title: National Day flypast means brief KLIA flight pauses – here’s when
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) today announced the closure of airspace within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area from Aug 26 to 29, and Aug 31 to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day flypast in Putrajaya. The airspace closure schedule for rehearsals and the National Day Flypast 2026 is as follows: From Aug 26 to 28, the airspace will be closed from 11am to noon for rehearsals. On Aug 31, the National Day Flypast will take place from 8.45 am to 9.45 am.

items.title: When losing money is winning: Selangor's plastic bag charges plummet
items.summary: State Public Health and Environment Exco Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the total collection in 2024 was recorded at RM9.04 million, bringing the total collection for the period 2023 to 2025 to RM29.36 million. “Based on these developments, the state government believes that the Plastic-Free Campaign and the Plastic Bag Charge Collection Programme have succeeded in raising public awareness and encouraging the use of reusable bags. “The trend of decreasing plastic bag charge collection also shows a change in consumer behavior towards reducing the use of single-use plastic bags,” she said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly Session today.

items.title: More than nine-tenths of Kelantan land remains Malay reserve, top in peninsula, says MB
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The total area of Malay reserve land in Kelantan is recorded at 526,083 hectares (ha) or 91.5 per cent, involving 816,020 ownerships as of June this year. According to Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, the area of non-Malay reserve land is 48,344 ha or 8.4 per cent, involving 43,255 titles. “Based on land administration records up to June 2026, the total area of land ownership in Kelantan is 574,427 ha, involving 859,275 titles.

items.title: Minister Zulkifli Hasan: Tabung Haji to face tougher oversight as govt acts on RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The government’s pledge to leave no stone unturned in strengthening Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) through stricter policy and regulatory measures to ensure that similar issues do not recur was among the messages at yesterday’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said a task force was established to examine the RCI’s findings and recommendations when tabling the report. It will be headed by TH chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain and comprises Bank Negara Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour and Securities Commission (SC) chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi.

items.title: PMX expected home today after hernia procedure, says wife
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to be discharged from hospital today after receiving treatment, his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said. She said Anwar expressed his appreciation to everyone who had prayed for his health and well-being. “PMX sends his regards and thanked everyone who has prayed for his health and recovery,” she said.

items.title: Six schools in Sarawak shift to online learning as haze hits ‘very unhealthy’ levels
items.summary: The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the precautionary measure was taken in line with the Education Ministry’s (MOE) guidelines, with the safety, health and wellbeing of students and school staff given priority. As of 10.30am today, the schools involved are SK Sejijag, with 51 students and 14 staff; SK Sungai Sameran (129 students, 21 staff); SK Tepoi (42 students, 15 staff); SK Entubuh (67 students, 18 staff); SK Temong (205 students, 21 staff); and SK Tema (85 students, 15 staff). According to JPNS, these schools are under the administration of the Serian District Education Office (Serian PPD).

items.title: One of two boys missing after river dip in Kuala Krai found dead, search continues for second 14-year-old (VIDEO)
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The body of one of two 14-year-old boys who went missing while bathing in a river in Kampung Batu Lada, Aur Duri, Kuala Krai, yesterday was found today. The body of Luth Naiman Mohd Noraziron was found by members of the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) of the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department at 9.10 am, about 100 metres from the incident site. It said today’s operation involved 56 personnel from the JBPM, police, Volunteer Fire Brigades and local residents.

items.title: Selangor Rail Line still in planning stage, completion targeted for 2060
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — The Selangor government is still in the discussion stage with various parties including the private sector to identify the appropriate development and financing model for the development of the Selangor Rail Line. State Investment, Trade and Mobility Exco Ng Sze Han said the state government through the Menteri Besar of Selangor (Incorporated) or MBI as the Technical Committee for Selangor Rail Development is examining the most potential development and financing model to be implemented. He said the mechanism for implementing the development of the Selangor Rail Line is also being refined to identify the most profitable and appropriate method.

items.title: MEF urges govt to act faster before MSME cash crunch turns into job losses
items.summary: MEF president Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman has proposed that the government consider introducing a coordinated MSME survival and resilience package to help businesses navigate ongoing cost and cash-flow pressures. He said the package should include targeted and temporary tax relief, faster and simpler access to financing and greater use of cash-flow-based lending. “Under this package, the government should consider expanding government-backed guarantees, temporary regulatory and compliance relief, faster payments to MSME suppliers, greater MSME access to government procurement and employment retention support,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Wong Chen joins Bersama after resigning as Subang MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Former Subang MP Wong Chen has joined Bersama, days after resigning from his parliamentary seat. Wong, a three-term MP who had been with PKR for nearly two decades, had previously indicated that he would eventually leave the party after Rafizi and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad resigned their parliamentary seats to lead Bersama. The other two were Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung.

items.title: Waiting for your university offer? UPUOnline results out Aug 14 noon
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The results of applications for further studies at public universities (UA) via UPUOnline® for the Bachelor’s Degree level for the 2026/2027 Academic Session for STPM/equivalent holders will be announced on August 14. Results can be checked from 12 noon, August 14 to 5 pm, August 23 online via the links https://upu.mohe.gov.my, https://upu2.mohe.gov.my and via the Mobile UPUPocket or Mobile MyGov applications on smartphones. “Only applicants who are unsuccessful in receiving an offer can submit an appeal application via UPUOnline® for admission to UA at https://upu.mohe.gov.my within 10 days from August 14 to 23,” said the Ministry of Education.

items.title: Federal Court dismisses Kedah govt’s bid for leave to appeal in pool betting outlet licences case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 (Bernama) -- The Federal Court today dismissed the Kedah state government’s application seeking leave to appeal against a ruling that had quashed its decision to cease the issuance and renewal of business licences for pool betting operators in the state. The Kedah Government had sought leave to appeal the Court of Appeal 2-1 majority decision, which upheld the High Court’s ruling in favour of pool betting agents, companies and their principal officers in challenging the state government’s directive. In the majority decision, Court of Appeal judge Datuk Faizah Jamaluddin said the decision by the state government to stop issuing and renewing pool betting business licences had exceeded the constitutional limits of the state power.

items.title: High Court orders Rosmah to pay RM67.4m into stakeholder account pending appeal in missing jewellery suit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor was today ordered by the High Court to pay RM67.4 million into a joint stakeholder account within a month, pending her appeal in a suit filed by Lebanese jeweller Global Royalty Trading SAL to recover the value of 43 jewellery items delivered to her. Rosmah had previously sought to stay the execution of the High Court’s June 10 decision, with the court having fixed today to deliver its decision on the application. “In the circumstances, the Court orders that a conditional stay of execution be granted to the defendant pending her appeal to the Court of Appeal.
